sources.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 author-hosted revision, 236 pp.)

Read from the fetched revision, with the derivation text, the plane-wave amplitude constraints, the polarisation classification with the handedness convention, and the averaged-flux computation inspected in full; \u00a74.3.3 and the remainder of \u00a74.4's later sections were read only to the extent needed to record their disposition.

contents.support: The source derivation is exactly the scaffolded route: differentiate Faraday in time, substitute Ampere, use the curl-curl identity and the Gauss constraints. The scaffold fixes the regularity ($C^2$), the SI constants and the source-free region, and records the failure of the converse that the source does not mention.

contents.name: \u00a74.3.1 pp. 84-87: the general profile solutions $f(x-ct)+g(x+ct)$; the monochromatic ansatz $E=E_0\sin(kx-\omega t)$; the dispersion relation $\omega^2=c^2k^2$; $B=(E_0/c)\sin(kx-\omega t)$ orthogonal to both $E$ and $k$; the principle of superposition; the complex-exponential encoding with the warning that quadratic quantities require the real part
contents.support: The scaffolded definition fixes $k\ne0$, $\omega>0$, complex amplitudes, the phase sign and the $C^\infty$ encoding exactly as the source's (4.15)-(4.17), and repeats the source's warning by asserting no quadratic interpretation.

contents.name: \u00a74.3.1 p. 86: 'the principle of superposition' - any sum of monochromatic solutions is a solution, which lets waves travelling in different directions pass through one another
contents.support: The two-wave superposition clause (a) of the scaffolded theorem is exactly this linearity, stated as a specialisation of the run's [[pthm-em-linear-superposition]]; the source sentence is absorbed there rather than built as a separate item.

contents.name: \u00a74.3.2 pp. 87-88: the fixed-frequency ansatz (4.18) and its amplitude constraints $ik\cdot E_0=0$, $ik\cdot B_0=0$, $ik\times E_0=i\omega B_0$ (no further constraint from the fourth equation); real amplitudes give linear polarisation with the right-handed triad $\hat k,E_0/c,B_0$; $E_0=\alpha-i\beta$ gives circular polarisation with the right-handed convention $\beta=\hat k\times\alpha$ and the general elliptic trace; the general Fourier wave with $\omega=ck$
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem states precisely the four amplitude equations, the dispersion relation and the transverse/orthogonality conclusions; the source's 'no further constraint' remark is the converse direction of clause (a). The polarisation classification and its handedness convention are carried by the companion definition item.

contents.name: \u00a74.3.2 pp. 87-88: classification of polarisations (linear for real amplitudes, circular for $|\alpha|=|\beta|$ with $\alpha\cdot\beta=0$, general elliptic) and the handedness convention $\beta=\hat k\times\alpha$
contents.support: The scaffolded definition states the trace $a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$ in the same convention, the three cases, and fixes the same handedness sign (translated to $H=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle<0$ for right-handed), with the naming caveat recorded explicitly.

contents.name: §4.3.3 pp. 89–91: normal and oblique plane-wave reflection off an ideal conductor, reflected fields and induced surface current, with angle of incidence equal to angle of reflection
contents.reason: Tong's section constructs reflected E and B fields at an ideal conducting half-space and obtains an induced surface current from the tangential magnetic jump; it does not apply the electrostatic method of image charges. The approved inventory excludes this additional explicit flat-PEC reflection/current application, consistently with the owning batch34 normal and oblique conductor exclusions. The actual pthm-em-phase-matching reflection-angle result and Fresnel constructions assume two lossless scalar dielectric media with finite positive permittivities and permeabilities and stated interface conditions; they do not supply the source's PEC problem. Existing dielectric reflection, finite-Ohmic skin depth, radiation-pressure reflector model and PEC guide/cavity claims remain intact.

contents.name: \u00a74.4 pp. 92-94: the field energy density and Poynting vector, $dU/dt=-\oint S\cdot dA-\int J\cdot E$, the plane-wave $S=(E_0^2/(c\mu_0))\hat k\sin^2(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, the period averages $\bar S=E_0^2/(2c\mu_0)\hat k$, $\bar u=\epsilon_0E_0^2/2$ and $\bar S=c\bar u\hat k$, and the local continuity equation $\partial_tE+\nabla\cdot S=0$
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem computes exactly these period averages for a general complex amplitude, with the tensor momentum-flux refinement; the source's local continuity equation (source-free case) is consumed there through [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], whose pair owns the general balance.

contents.name: \u00a75.6 pp. 127-133: momentum density $P=\epsilon_0E\times B$, the Maxwell stress tensor, its balance equation and the covariant energy-momentum tensor
contents.reason: These results are the subject of the earlier companion pair em-energy-momentum-and-angular-balance (order 343) built in batch 32, which this page consumes for $\sigma$, $g$ and the balance identities; the covariant tensor is deferred to the Lorentz-covariant formulation page as recorded there.

contents.name: \u00a74.3.4, the historical Asides (Maxwell, Faraday, and the aether discussion in \u00a75.1) and the quantum/optical applications beyond the plane-wave analysis
contents.reason: Historical and motivational narrative with no mathematical content used by this pair, and the quantum/optical applications belong to frameworks outside classical electromagnetism; citing them would add no premise, proof step or qualification to any scaffolded item.

sources.title: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 3rd edition (Prentice Hall, 1999, 596-page retained scan)
sources.locator: \u00a79.2.1 'The Wave Equation for E and B' printed pp. 375-376, \u00a79.2.2 'Monochromatic Plane Waves' printed pp. 376-379, and \u00a79.2.3 'Energy and Momentum in Electromagnetic Waves' printed pp. 381-382, with Problems 9.10-9.12 on printed p. 382 of the retained 596-page scan (13 484 424 bytes). Printed p. 380 of this scan has no extractable text layer; it was not read and no scaffolded claim rests on it. The wave-equation derivation, the plane-wave constraints, the averages, the radiation-pressure statement and the averaging and stress-tensor problems were read in full on the pages listed.

contents.name: \u00a79.2.1 printed pp. 375-376: in source-free regions the curl of Faraday's and Ampere's laws gives $\nabla^2E=\mu_0\epsilon_0\,\partial^2E/\partial t^2$ and the $B$ analogue, so each Cartesian component satisfies the wave equation with speed $v=1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}=c$
contents.support: Same derivation as the scaffolded theorem; the scaffold adds the precise $C^2$ hypothesis, the curl-curl identity reference and the explicit statement that only necessity is claimed.

contents.name: \u00a79.2.2 printed pp. 376-379: the monochromatic plane-wave ansatz (9.43); the explicit warning that every empty-space Maxwell solution obeys the wave equation 'but the converse is not true; Maxwell's equations impose extra constraints'; the transversality $(E_0)_z=(B_0)_z=0$ from the divergence equations; Faraday's law giving $B_0=(1/c)(\hat k\times E_0)$ with $E$, $B$ in phase, mutually perpendicular and transverse; the polarisation convention
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem's clauses (a)-(c) are exactly these constraints and conclusions with complex amplitudes; its clause (d) and [[pthm-em-vacuum-wave-equation]](b) record the source's converse warning as a scope exclusion.

contents.name: \u00a79.2.2 printed pp. 376-379: the definition of the monochromatic plane wave as the paradigmatic solution with complex amplitudes whose real parts are the fields
contents.support: The scaffolded definition is the same encoding on the whole-space region with the phase sign fixed, the terminology ($k$, $\omega$, period, amplitudes) supplied, and no field equation asserted.

contents.name: \u00a79.2.3 printed pp. 381-382: momentum density $P=S/c^2$ for the monochromatic wave; cycle averages $\langle u\rangle=\frac12\epsilon_0E_0^2$, $\langle S\rangle=\frac12c\epsilon_0E_0^2\hat k$ and $\langle P\rangle=\frac12(\epsilon_0E_0^2/c)\hat k$; intensity $I=\langle S\rangle$
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem states the averages for a general complex amplitude and adds the averaged stress/momentum-flux tensor identity, with the same normalisation $\epsilon_0cE_0^2/2$ for a real linear amplitude; the balance reading cites the two balance theorems of the run.

contents.name: \u00a79.2.3 printed p. 382: radiation pressure on a perfect absorber is $1/c$ times the incident momentum flux, and twice as great on a perfect reflector; the qualitative $qv\times B$ mechanism
contents.support: The scaffolded thought experiment derives the same two pressure values from the averaged momentum flux of the page under explicitly stated idealisations (vanishing field on the material side, pillbox force law) and states that no measured pressure or material law is claimed.

contents.name: Problem 9.11 printed p. 382: the same-$(k,\omega)$ averaging device $\langle fg\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{Re}(f\bar g)$ and its applications to $\langle u\rangle$ and $\langle S\rangle$
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem performs exactly this averaging through the run's [[lem-em-period-average]] (stated for real parts of complex exponentials with the same frequency), so the problem's algebraic content is absorbed into the proof rather than scaffolded as a separate item.

contents.name: Problem 9.12 printed p. 382: all elements of the Maxwell stress tensor for a linearly polarised monochromatic plane wave, and the relation of the momentum-flux density to the energy density
contents.support: Clause (c) of the scaffolded theorem proves the general complex-amplitude form $\langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle=-\langle u\rangle\hat k_i\hat k_j$ (equivalently $\langle\Pi_{ij}\rangle=\langle u\rangle\hat k_i\hat k_j$), of which the problem's linearly polarised case is the real-amplitude specialisation.

contents.name: Problem 9.10 printed p. 382: the numerical sunlight-intensity exercise for absorber and reflector pressures
contents.reason: A numerical exercise quoting an ambient intensity; this pair reports no empirical data, and adopting a natural constant or a measured irradiance would import an empirical premise that the framework's experiment items must source and qualify separately.

contents.name: \u00a79.3 onward printed pp. 382 ff.: electromagnetic waves in matter, reflection and transmission at interfaces, and guided waves
contents.reason: The material response (constitutive laws, dispersion, conducting media) and boundary-value reflection/transmission problems are supplied by em-wave-interfaces-and-conductors and em-waveguides-and-cavities, which follow this pair in the plan and declare the needed material postulates; they are not premises of the vacuum wave and polarisation claims.
